instant_learning__measured_controlled.claim: the engine learns a fix from one repair and reuses it on the next
instant_learning__measured_controlled.experiment: the SAME two bugs, run once against an EMPTY skill store and once against the warm store
instant_learning__measured_controlled.effect: 7x fewer candidates evaluated, 1.98x faster wall clock, same verified result
instant_learning__measured_controlled.why_this_is_instant_learning_and_not_tra: no parameter is fitted. The skill store is a SQLite table of verified (skeleton fingerprint -> repair pattern) pairs. A repair is crystallised only after it verifies against the tests. The store is read at inference; it is never trained.

measured.throughput: 100 reset+act cycles in 12.9 ms = 0.13 ms per environment action

what_is_still_NOT_real: no SWE-bench score. The 2/2 is two small cases authored here, with controls, not 300 real GitHub issues.
no OSWorld score. The GUI half needs a real OS; the documentation says so and so does this record.
ARC-AGI stays at 1.5 percent with four measured flat attempts.
no Opus 5.5 parity on any open-domain benchmark.
the heldout language corpus from earlier is spent.
the_honest_shape_of_the_answer: this project is not a worse Claude. It is a different machine: strong exactly where a claim can be verified by execution, and refusing everywhere else. That is why 2/2 on multi-file repair with zero model calls is a real result and 1.5 percent on ARC is a real ceiling. Both are true and neither is a parity claim.
